articles.title: Russian vessel hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Libya’s Benghazi port
articles.excerpt:
A suspected sea drone attack has hit a Russian vessel in eastern Libya, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to the North African country’s eastern-based government.

Local sources told Al...
articles.body_text:
A suspected sea drone attack has hit a Russian vessel in eastern Libya, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to the North African country’s eastern-based government.

Local sources told Al Jazeera late on Sunday that an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed in the attack at dawn, adding that the ship was moored inside the civil sea port of Benghazi, close to a naval base.

The sources said the ship was carrying weapons, ammunition and drones in its cargo. Local sources quoted residents as saying that they saw three drones attack the vessel.

Satellite imagery provider Vantor said imagery showed the vessel was the Merkury, a Russian Navy corvette, or small warship.

Imagery taken on Sunday showed that most of the vessel ‌had capsized and sunk, with only its bow still visible above water. Smoke was also visible rising from part of the ship’s superstructure, with significant debris scattered along the pier.

The Benghazi-based administration earlier said the vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement between Russia and Libya’s eastern government.

Late on Sunday, the AP news agency quoted unnamed sources as saying that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya.

Also on Sunday evening, another sea drone hit a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack. The Benghazi-administration’s Health Ministry said all crew members “who were injured when a merchant vessel was targeted this evening by explosives-laden sea drones off the coast of Benghazi” had been rescued and were receiving treatment.

No further details were given. The Almasar satellite television channel said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.

The Benghazi-based administration said it had launched a joint investigation with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it”.

The government said the fire had been brought under control and the site secured, while it condemned the suspected strike as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety.

“The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said, adding that Libya was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities in the Black Sea.

On Saturday, a drone struck a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea near Finnish waters. Finland’s border guard attributed the strike to Ukraine.

A Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast in March after an attack that Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed on Ukraine, while last December, Ukraine said it had used aerial drones to strike a Russian-linked oil tanker in the Mediterranean.

Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011.

A United Nations-recognised government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration is in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.

articles.title: Australian politics live: Labor to extend PBS medicine freeze to 2030; Bowen ‘failed’ on Cop, Hume says
articles.excerpt:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese is back in the country after appearances at international summits in China and the Philippines.

He has called a press con...
articles.body_text:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese is back in the country after appearances at international summits in China and the Philippines.

He has called a press conference to announce the government will introduce legislation to keep PBS-listed medication priced at $25 until the end of the decade.

Labor is under significant pressure as the cost of living rises – so the PM is hopeful this will bring some relief to both household purses and his government.

double quotation markToday we will introduce legislation to extend the freeze of the cost of PBS medicines at just $25 until the end of the decade.

This helps Australians now with the cost of medicines but it helps to keep our nation healthier as well, and we understand the cost of essential medicines can put pressure on household budgets and that’s why we’re giving Australians access to cheaper medicines.

Under the former government, when we came to office, PBS co-payments soared, but now medicines would have cost over $50 per script for general patients.

Don’t ‘jump at shadows’: Albanese bats off defence bill criticism

Anthony Albanese has tried to bat off concern over a defence bill that critics warn could have serious implications for democracy.

My colleague Sarah Basford Canales explains the situation here:

The long and the short of it is the government, with the support of the Coalition, will pass a bill that will criminalise photographs of defence sites and give security officials the ability to search and detain people suspected of trying to enter designated zones.

The Greens and civil rights groups warn that could capture peaceful protesters and other civilians standing outside defence zones.

Albanese is dismissive of the criticisms:

double quotation markPeople shouldn’t jump at shadows, and that is what I’ve seen some of the commentary at doing, reaching absurd proportions. It will be accountable, obviously, for things that are designated, but we live in unsafe times.

I find it remarkable in 2026 as a question over whether we need to designate areas as being protected and we live in times where we know there are more conflicts in the world today than at any time since World War II.

Cop breakdown evidence of ‘difficult geopolitical times’: Albanese

The prime minister has been forced to defend Australia’s central involvement in the Cop climate talks that broke down and could not reach consensus.

Anthony Albanese says it’s “evidence that we’re living in difficult geopolitical times”.

But he continues to back the involvement, saying it was necessary to remain a key player in the Pacific.

double quotation markClimate change is the first, second, and third priority of Pacific leaders. It is an existential threat to countries such as Tuvalu and Kiribati, who we have continued to engage with and build relationships. But there’s a link as well between environmental security and national security. You’ll see some of that played out this week. In order to have credibility, the entry fee is action on climate change.

Private health insurance legislation being negotiated in ‘good faith’

Keeping PBS medications to $25 is likely to be a slam dunk for the government – it’s politically easy policy.

A much trickier battle is ahead though, with the government still searching for support to increase private health insurance rebates for over 65s. The Coalition have said there’s no shot they will support that bill.

The health minister, Mark Butler, says the government is negotiating in good faith with the Greens – who want pensioners carved out.

double quotation markWe’re in negotiations with the Greens party. Have been over the last little while and, yes, we would hope to have that legislation dealt with in the Senate this week.

We conduct negotiations under this prime minister in good faith. We listen to the Senate. We understand we don’t have the numbers in the Senate to pass this bill right now in the form that we introduced it. So, of course, we’re negotiating to see what we can achieve.

Anthony Albanese is back in the country after appearances at international summits in China and the Philippines.

He has called a press conference to announce the government will introduce legislation to keep PBS-listed medication priced at $25 until the end of the decade.

Labor is under significant pressure as the cost of living rises – so the PM is hopeful this will bring some relief to both household purses and his government.

double quotation markToday we will introduce legislation to extend the freeze of the cost of PBS medicines at just $25 until the end of the decade.

This helps Australians now with the cost of medicines but it helps to keep our nation healthier as well, and we understand the cost of essential medicines can put pressure on household budgets and that’s why we’re giving Australians access to cheaper medicines.

Under the former government, when we came to office, PBS co-payments soared, but now medicines would have cost over $50 per script for general patients.

New nest of red imported fire ants found and destroyed in Sydney

The NSW government discovered a new nest of red imported fire ants in Sydney over the weekend, with findings suggesting the nest could be about a year old.

Officials destroyed the colony, found in Auburn in the city’s west, after it was deemed to contained red imported fire ants, a major invasive species that poses threats to both human health and the environment.

A separate nest was discovered two months ago at the Enfield logistics centre, more than 6km from the site found this weekend. The new nest was found outside a biosecurity control zone and officials are investigating if it is a different infestation originating from another source. Detection dogs are set to be on site soon and a new biosecurity control order is being developed.

Tara Moriarty, the NSW minister for agriculture, said:

double quotation markHuman movement of materials is the primary way fire ants spread, which is why we’re asking everyone to stay alert and report anything suspicious.

Everyone has a part to play in biosecurity, and I thank the member of the public for reporting this site in Auburn.

The Coalition’s big problem now is that they’re worried the scheme creates an oversupply of gas in the domestic market by design, which would lower gas prices.

They say that could deter new gas investment or even lead to gas slowly dying off.

Hume says the government has already made key concessions by carving out WA, so she’s hopeful there can be a deal.

double quotation markWe want a gas reservation. We’ve been saying that from the start but it can’t be at any price. The government has moved a long way. I think the carveout of WA was a significant move and a good start. But there’s more that can be done.

We want to make sure that we get the calibration of this right. We can’t afford an oversupply domestically that would have detrimental effects on prices for investors. We need new gas in the system, more gas in the system, more investment in gas.

Jane Hume has not missed an opportunity to stick the knife into Chris Bowen after the UN Cop summit failed to reach a consensus after historically long talks.

Sitting in the hot seat after Murray Watt in the RN Breakfast studio, Hume says Bowen failed overseas, while Australians have also faced rising energy prices.

double quotation markNot only has he failed in these negotiations as the lead negotiator but he’s also failed Australians at the time when he has spent $150m just to be there, just to get this presidency in the first place.

Our energy prices have gone up. Our emissions have flatlined. I think that’s kind of disappointing. He’s really got a job to do at home.

Labor wants gas reservation scheme passed this week

Labor is trying its hand at playing off the Coalition and Greens to get its gas reservation scheme through this week.

The environment minister, Murray Watt, says the Coalition was the party most likely to support the legislation but is now being a bit “intransigent” so Labor could instead make a deal with the Greens.

At face value it looks like a tactic to try to strong-arm the Coalition back to the negotiation table because it’s a policy similar to what they themselves had proposed before the last election under Peter Dutton.

And the government has already made a major concession by carving out WA from the scheme.

double quotation markI think, up until last week, we certainly felt that the Coalition was the more likely party but we’re seeing the same kind of intransigence from them that we saw last year with the EPBC reforms. But this week is an important week and this is the week that the Coalition can decide if they support cheaper gas. That’s certainly the intention.

I think it’s also worth noting one other group that has evaded scrutiny on this is Pauline Hanson’s One Nation party. They have traditionally supported a gas reservation but, mysteriously, shortly after Gina Rinehart, who’s a big gas producer, has supported their party, they’ve flipped their position.

My colleague Sarah Martin wrote about this policy flip a couple of months ago:

‘Very difficult to bridge that divide’: Murray Watt

Cabinet minister Murray Watt says it’s increasingly difficult to bridge the divide between nations on climate policy after a frustrating Cop summit that didn’t reach a final agreement.

Speaking to ABC’s Radio National, the environment minister says it wasn’t a failure and points to the fact that the US didn’t even send an official delegation.

On the proposed deal not including the words “fossil fuels”, Watt says there were a range of nations that weren’t prepared to sign up if they were included … but in omitting them found another group of countries that refused to agree anyway.

double quotation markIt’s obviously a very deeply disappointing outcome that the cover decision was not agreed to by all nations.

I think what this shows is a very challenging international environment at the moment to reach agreement on almost anything and particularly a situation like this where you’ve got fossil fuel producers on the one hand and other countries that are experiencing very serious impacts from climate change.

That’s a very wide divide to be bridged and it’s very disappointing that that wasn’t possible.

US foreign policy influence falls in Asia Power Index

Serial blunders have caused the foreign policy sway of Australia’s most important ally, the US, to plummet on the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index, AAP reports.

The US led China in six of the survey’s eight criteria but trailed on diplomatic influence and economic relationships, while Washington’s foreign policy score posted its sharpest decline in the index’s nine-year history.

Anthony Albanese earned praise for inking deals with Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei to avert a fuel supply crisis caused by the war but his government scored much lower on advancing Australia’s diplomatic interests in Asia.

The institute’s report also comes on the heels of the prime minister pinballing between Turkey, the Philippines and China for the Cop31, Asean and Apec summits.

Albanese signed up to joint military exercises with Quad partners the US, Japan and India, and on Friday was lauded by the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, for achieving a “full turnaround” in Sino-Australian relations.

Researcher Jack Sato, who helped compile the annual report, said the week’s developments underlined some of the power index’s more optimistic findings.

double quotation markWe’re seeing much greater defence engagement between Australia and Japan, Australia and the Philippines, and the Philippines and Japan.

Even though I think it doesn’t quite come across in its overall score, that US defence relationship in the region is stronger, which is helping Australia.

‘It’s frustrating we didn’t get further’: Plibersek

The social services minister, Tanya Plibersek, has conceded it is “frustrating” that nations at Cop didn’t get a deal over the line but defended Australia leading the talks.

Speaking to Sunrise, before the panel with One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce devolved into a slanging match, Plibersek said it was crucial all countries came to the table:

double quotation markI’m sure Barnaby would agree, if we’re going to take action to reduce carbon emissions, Australia can’t be the only country doing it.

It’s frustrating that we didn’t get further. I’m sure Chris [Bowen] is, you know, the most frustrated person I can think of right now because he put in many hours.

Just like the atmosphere, the temperature rises – and the two start arguing with each other over policy and cost.

Joyce says One Nation wants to “get away from your [Labor] policy which is destroying our nation”, while Plibersek asks him to say what the cost will be under his policy that would see more fossil fuels burned.

‘Pretty extraordinary’: Liberals blast Cop negotiations

The Liberals say it’s extraordinary the government put its hand up to co-host the UN climate summit in Turkey and failed to secure an agreement between nations.

It’s despite the summit going overtime to continue negotiations, making it the longest COP ever.

The EU, UK and some allies rejected a deal on the future of the climate which didn’t even mention fossil fuels.

The deputy Liberal leader says voters should be concerned Australia couldn’t broker a deal. Jane Hume told News24:

double quotation markIt’s pretty extraordinary, isn’t it? We’ve spent $150m to get Chris Bowen to Cop, to host Cop. Then we found out it was actually a co-host deal. Now we’re walking away without a deal at all. This is quite extraordinary.

It hasn’t been, since 2009, when Kevin Rudd was in Copenhagen, that we had no agreement, but to have no deal at all, this is quite exceptional, and I think it should be something that Australia should be concerned about.

The Cop co-president, climate change minister, Chris Bowen, defended his leadership.

“Australia left nothing on the field,” he said, but the red lines the presidencies had tried to negotiate were “unbridgeable”.

Good morning, Krishani Dhanji here with you for the final sitting week of the year! (Don’t sound too excited.)

It’s crunch time for Labor who have several key pieces of legislation they want to pass this week including digital duty of care, the gas reservation scheme, changes to capital gains tax for trusts, and reducing private health insurance premiums for over 65s.

So far they’re closer to a deal on the first two, trusts is somewhere in between, and private health is looking iffy – but anything is possible.

Labor is also going to cop some heat (get it!) after climate talks broke down at the UN Cop summit where the energy minister, Chris Bowen, was the chief negotiator.

I’ve got my coffee, I hope you’ve got yours – let’s get stuck in.

Anthony Albanese returns from a series of overseas summits to crunch negotiations on multiple proposed changes as his popularity takes a further nosedive, as Australian Associated Press reports.

The Labor leader trails his opposition counterpart, Angus Taylor, as preferred prime minister for the first time, according to a Newspoll published in The Australian on Monday.

Albanese’s net approval rating also hit a new low of minus 31, while the Coalition managed to claw back some voter support. Its primary vote stood at 22% in the latest survey, behind One Nation and Labor, which were tied on 27%.

Wong warns about AI in major foreign policy speech

AI is a foreign policy and national security challenge, Penny Wong will tell parliament this week, raising concerns in a major speech about how the growing technology is being used in war and foreign interference.

Wong will give a substantial foreign policy address to parliament on Tuesday, with advance speech notes detailing a focus on artificial intelligence. The foreign affairs minister will warn that AI tools “make that [foreign] interference faster, cheaper and harder to recognise”.

Wong says Australia welcomes investment in AI but urged a focus on safety - particularly on the international stage.

double quotation markWe must do what we can to ensure that the race to develop frontier AI, concentrated in a handful of companies and countries, does not reward speed over prudence.

Australia has helped shape the international order before, in non-proliferation and in online safety. With artificial intelligence, we intend to do it again.

Anika Wells said the government would consult on how to exempt low-risk small businesses – and potentially other services – from the digital duty of care legislation before it comes into effect 12 months later.

Business groups had called for such a change but the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry had urged that it be specifically included in the legislation, not worked out later via regulation. Its chief executive, Andrew McKellar, said:

double quotation markA small business should not have to engage lawyers simply to work out whether its website is caught by a regime carrying penalties of more than $100m. The answer should be in black and white in the legislation.

The Greens are expected to eventually back the bill but more negotiations will continue this week.

Labor will exempt small businesses from its digital duty of care legislation – a key request from business groups, and potentially another step toward getting the bill passed.

The government is still seeking the support of the Greens on the bill, who want tougher penalties.

The carveout for small businesses from new regulations was not at the top of the Greens’ agenda – they also want a new ombudsman for big tech – but the new update from the communications minister, Anika Wells, shows Labor is in the mood to make deals.

double quotation markThe intention of the digital duty of care is to put the onus on tech companies to protect Australians from online harms before they occur – not to create additional burden for low-risk small businesses.

A low-risk website for a cafe or bookkeeper is unlikely to cause harm to its users so, once the digital duty of care starts, they will be exempt from the law. We will work closely with small business to get the setting right.

Good morning and welcome to Guardian Australia’s coverage of Australian politics. Krishani Dhanji will be with us shortly.

articles.title: Jennifer Lopez claims not being a ‘typical’ White actress made it harder to land Hollywood movie roles
articles.excerpt:
Jennifer Lopez attends the 2026 Netflix Upfront at Sunset Pier 94 Studios in New York City on May 13, 2026. (John Nacion/WireImage)

Jennifer Lopez is receiving criticism after claiming that she has s...
articles.body_text:
Jennifer Lopez attends the 2026 Netflix Upfront at Sunset Pier 94 Studios in New York City on May 13, 2026. (John Nacion/WireImage)

Jennifer Lopez is receiving criticism after claiming that she has struggled to land acting roles in Hollywood because she is not White, describing how she has been forced to create her "own lane" as a Latina entertainer, in an interview published on Friday.

Lopez made the remarks in an interview with The New York Times, pushing back on the notion that she gets thousands of acting offers, claiming instead that Hollywood has often overlooked her because of her ethnicity.

"Even from the beginning of my career, I got offered things, but I was only offered a few things. I had to kind of create things for myself," the actress said. "And the reason, I think, is because I just wasn't the typical kind of, like, to be honest, a White actress. You know what I mean? And it's still kind of the same today."

'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER YEARS OF REJECTION AND ‘ABUSE’

Jennifer Lopez posing in a sheer dress at the Golden Globe Awards in Los Angeles in January 2026. (Christopher Polk/2026GG/Penske Media via Getty Images)

Lopez’s more recent film credits include "Office Romance" (2026), "Shotgun Wedding" (2022), "Hustlers" (2019) and "Second Act" (2018).

She also secured several leading roles in the late 1990s and early 2000s, including "The Wedding Planner," "Out of Sight" and "Maid in Manhattan," and was cast as the late singer Selena Quintanilla-Perez in "Selena."

JENNIFER LOPEZ ADMITS SHE 'WOULD'VE HAD SEX' WITH ENTIRE STAR-STUDDED 90S MOVIE CAST

The Puerto Rican actress said Hollywood continues to look for "certain" things when casting performers, suggesting that the industry's preferences have historically made it more difficult for actors of color to secure roles.

Lopez acknowledged, however, that the screen industry has made progress in improving diversity and representation.

Jennifer Lopez and Brett Goldstein are seen on the set of their film Office Romance on April 7, 2025, in Hoboken, New Jersey. (Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

"There's a certain thing that they look for, and it's more diverse now for sure, and that's good," the actress said.

"But because of that, you have to kind of create your own lane in a lot of ways," she added. "If I want to do something, I don't wait for somebody to offer me…I try to do it, and then if something comes along, great."

IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE

Fox News co-host Tomi Lahren pushed back on Lopez’s claims, writing on X: "LOL, sure Jan."

Internet personality Oli London noted Lopez’ robust net worth and catalog of big-screen appearances, writing on X: "JLO has appeared in 44 films and is worth $400 million."

Actress and "America's Next Top Model" personality Adrianne Curry-Rhode also chimed in, calling Lopez' comments "next level delusion."

"You are old now. You were a bad actress, but very hot...that's why you got casted," Curry-Rhode wrote in a post to X.

Movie critic Christian Toto told Fox News Digital, "Lopez has worked steadily over the past two decades, bouncing from major film projects to concerts and her solo music career. She's undeniably talented and has earned every gig that came her way. Still, for her to suggest she's been penalized by Hollywood for the color of her skin is absurd. How many out-of-work actors would kill to snag a fraction of the work Hollywood has sent her way?"

Nora Moriarty is a Writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
articles.excerpt:
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud...
articles.body_text:
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.

If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

articles.title: Solo diners are asking restaurants for half-size portions, sparking debate over menu flexibility
articles.excerpt: Outnumbered discusses whether solo dining is lonely or liberating as OpenTable reports a 23% rise in reservations for one and an average spend of $94. Panelists share personal experiences and debate t...
articles.body_text:
Outnumbered discusses whether solo dining is lonely or liberating as OpenTable reports a 23% rise in reservations for one and an average spend of $94. Panelists share personal experiences and debate the implications of increased solo meals.

As solo dining continues to surge in popularity, there is debate over whether it’s acceptable for guests dining alone at a restaurant to request a smaller portion size of a dish.

Reservations for one saw a 22% increase year over year in the third quarter of 2025, according to a report from restaurant technology company Toast.

One appealing part of dining out with a group is sharing plates and trying bites of many different dishes.

RESTAURANTS DRAW THE LINE ON SUBSTITUTIONS AS DINERS PUSH MENU LIMITS

Solo diners who still want to sample a variety of items without having an overwhelming amount of food on their table may be able to do so by simply asking their server if they can place a half-order, Food & Wine reported.

Solo dining has surged in popularity in recent years, industry data shows. (iStock)

Opinions are divided online about whether this is an acceptable request, with some believing that it’s no big deal while others say it’s not worth it.

"Don't even bother, order the regular meal. And when it comes, you eat what you want of it, and anything that you have left over, get a to go box and take it home," one person wrote on Quora.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Many restaurants don’t appreciate when an adult orders a smaller portion size, the commenter added, saying, "they consider it to be a waste of their cooking time to make small portions for an adult."

Plus, they noted, it doesn't hurt to have leftovers.

Foods like pizza and whole fishes or meats may be more difficult for restaurants to scale down for solo diners.  (iStock)

Some chefs are happy to serve smaller portions to a solo diner because they want them to have a positive dining experience and be able to try many different dishes without wasting as much food, Food & Wine noted.

"It never hurts to ask!" another Quora user said, with the caveat that certain dishes are more easily re-portioned than others.

"Whether or not you are successful in your request depends on a few things. If the dish is pre-proportioned, then it’s not likely," they noted.

For example, if an entree contains a half lobster tail, it’s probably not likely that the kitchen will scale that component down, the commenter continued, adding that restaurants may refuse to serve whole fishes and meats, portioned desserts or pizzas in smaller sizes.

The important thing for diners to remember, they said, is that they will probably pay full price for a dish even if it’s a half-sized portion, because it takes an equal amount of time and effort to make.

Younger consumers, particularly Gen Z and millennials, are fueling the solo dining trend. (iStock)

One Reddit user agreed that the portion sizes of certain dishes are more easily adjusted than others.

"I think it’s easier with pasta dishes because they can portion out the amount of pasta, sauce, garnish, etc and keep selling the rest. Not so easy with a piece of protein (1/2 steak, 1/2 fish filet, 1/2 burger) because those are generally pre-portioned for service," they said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another person noted that they wanted a smaller portion to reduce food waste — and a smaller bill would be nice, too.

"I hate wasting food, but if I eat the full portion I’m overeating and will feel sick. I’d love to do a half portion for a slightly cheaper price and not overeat or waste food," they said.

One Redditor shared that they were pleasantly surprised when a restaurant they dined solo at charged them half of the menu price for a half-sized portion.

Sadie Chafe is a writer on the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
articles.excerpt: Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer Leag...
articles.body_text:
Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.

For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.

This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.

The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.

The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.

And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.

“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.

After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.

“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.

“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”

That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.

Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.

The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”

For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.

The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.

The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.

Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.

“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.

“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”

KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.

Rodman scored from a header minutes later.

The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.

Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.

Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.

“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.

“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”

Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.

And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.

The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.

Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.

On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.

For the Spirit, Rodman was a young, rising star at the last tournament, but she heads into next year as one of the most renowned players in the sport as the USWNT push to reclaim the title from Spain.

The Spirit’s number 10, Leicy Santos, is also set to shine on the international stage with Colombia, while defender Esme Morgan is likely to be called up for England. Sandy MacIver is expected to start between the sticks for Scotland.

Algeria’s Melissa Bethi could also feature at the tournament after her team secured qualification by reaching the WAFCON semifinals.

“One of the best things about DC is that it is an international city,” Bolt said.

“We love the fact that our team is a reflection of the city, the diversity of the city – that we have so many international players.”

articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries calls Trump chief of staff Stephen Miller a ‘stone-cold racist,’ refuses to sit down with him
articles.excerpt:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called White House chief of staff Stephen Miller a "stone-cold racist" and said he would never directly speak with him.

Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y....
articles.body_text:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called White House chief of staff Stephen Miller a "stone-cold racist" and said he would never directly speak with him.

Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., declared firmly on Saturday that he will not sit down with White House chief of staff Stephen Miller — calling Miller a "stone-cold racist" while mulling over who his conduit to the White House will be.

Jeffries, who is set to become House speaker in January, made the remarks during a recent podcast interview with The New York Times, in which he discussed ways he plans to work with the Trump administration to move forward legislation for the American people. When asked whether he imagined sitting across from Stephen Miller, Jeffries firmly said, "No," and disparaged the White House official.

"I've made it clear that Stephen Miller is a stone-cold racist. Why would I deal with him at this point in time?" Jeffries said.

TRUMP'S MOVE FROM WILES TO MILLER SIGNALS MAJOR TACTICAL SHIFT FOR GOVERNING WITHOUT CONGRESS

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries says he will not meet with White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, calling him a "stone-cold racist" over his immigration agenda. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images; Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Jeffries, who has historically been an outspoken critic of Miller, said he cannot meet with someone who has carried out such a violent immigration agenda.

"This is the architect, the architect of Donald Trump's violent mass deportation machine. And there's cruelty associated with that. There's chaos. In fact, there's death associated with what's taking place," Jeffries said.

In response to Fox News Digital, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers defended Miller's track record.

"Unlike the hardcore, partisan Democrats who refused to work with the President and blocked many of his popular policies, Stephen Miller has a track record of spearheading bipartisan efforts: public safety reform, making our cities such as Washington, D.C., and Memphis safe again, drug pricing transparency, and unleashing a nuclear energy renaissance," Rogers told Fox News Digital.

JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS

Earlier this month, President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller his new White House chief of staff, calling him one of his "most trusted advisors." (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

TRUMP TELLS DHS CHIEF TO WORK WITH DEMOCRATS ON IMMIGRATION REFORM, BUT NO AMNESTY

When President Donald Trump appointed Miller, Jeffries also blasted the president’s move as an "irresponsible decision" and condemned the chief of staff for his movement to "brutalize and kill American citizens," referencing the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good during immigration enforcement actions.

Trump defended the deportation agenda of his chief of staff pick at the time, telling Kayleigh McEnany on "Saturday in America" that, "The one thing with Stephen – he was very strong on the border."

"So, he called him a racist. But we had to be strong," Trump continued. "They allowed 25 million people and killers, murderers. They allowed drug dealers and rapists into our country."

The president also lauded Jeffries as a "very smart" and "reasonable guy."

"What he did is pretty spectacular with getting that position," Trump said. "And it’s nice – first Black person in that position. It’s a big deal."

THE MISTAKE NEWLY-ELECTED DEMS ADMIT THEY CAN'T AFFORD TO MAKE WITH TRUMP AFTER SWEEPING 2026 WINS

During an interview on "Saturday in America," President Trump lauded Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., as a "very smart" and "reasonable guy." (Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Jeffries insisted to The New York Times that his refusal to meet with Miller was "not a boycott," and expressed that he was willing to have an open communication line with Trump, just not Miller.

"I think practically speaking, one, I can communicate directly with the president," Jeffries told The New York Times. "I mean, everybody seems to have his number, but the president is not a hard person to reach."

Jeffries also said he can take his issues to Vice President JD Vance, explaining that in prior administrations, engagement between congressional leaders and the White House oftentimes happened via Cabinet secretaries or vice presidents.

"I wouldn't say I like any of the Cabinet secretaries within the Trump administration at this particular point in time," Jeffries said, adding that he has spoken with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The New York Democrat declared he will "maintain a willingness" to work with politicians across the aisle to get things done for the American people.

Jeffries’ office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Nora Moriarty is a Writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Week 12 AP Top 25 Poll sees Big Ten powers rightfully punished while Longhorns jump the Crimson Tide
articles.excerpt:
Former Michigan tight end held nothing back against the College Football Playoff committee and their strange rankings they've released so far.

After the Week 11 AP Top 25 poll was an anomaly, with th...
articles.body_text:
Former Michigan tight end held nothing back against the College Football Playoff committee and their strange rankings they've released so far.

After the Week 11 AP Top 25 poll was an anomaly, with the top nine teams going unchanged from the week prior, we returned to our regularly scheduled programming of utter chaos in college football and a lot of moving pieces in the newest edition of the AP Top 25 poll.

The Big Ten suffered some untimely cannibalization in Week 12, with Indiana, UCLA, and Ohio State all going on the road and losing, and all three teams were punished rather harshly as a result.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The SEC scoreboard featured nothing but chalk this past weekend, but with the Big Ten producing a mess, Texas has entered the Top 5 again, which can't be sitting all too well among Alabama fans.

GEORGIA HAS TOP COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF SEED IN SIGHT WITH DOMINATING ROAD WIN OVER NO 21 SOUTH CAROLINA

Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Austin Mack scrambles for yardage as Chattanooga Mocs defensive back Mason Bryant tries to tackle him during the first half at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., on Nov. 21, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

With voters being forced into putting out a fresh set of rankings every week for three consecutive months, they appear to have found their stride, at least as best they can. Remember, voters are spread out all around the country, in different time zones, making it physically impossible to watch even the extended highlights of every meaningful game on the slate.

With that in mind, there isn't a whole lot to get too worked up about when it comes to the upper echelon of this week's rankings.

UCLA has been a great story this season, and the sport is better when the Bruins are relevant, but they've undoubtedly felt like the team primed for a slip-up, and that coming to a Michigan team that is inept on offense is pretty peak college football.

The Bruins tumbling from No. 4 to No. 10 after having their unbeaten season ruined in Ann Arbor is fair. They're still a one-loss Big Ten team, and one-loss Big Ten teams deserve to remain inside the Top 10 this season.

LANE KIFFIN TAKES THE SIDE EXIT AS TENNESSEE SENDS LSU HOME AND MOVES TO THE DOORSTEP OF CFP

Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti is seen following a college football game between the Northwestern Wildcats and Indiana Hoosiers on Sept. 25, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Indiana went from a one-loss Big Ten team to a two-loss Big Ten team after an unsuccessful trip to Washington. The Hoosiers may only have one meaningful win all season – against USC in Week 11 – but their two losses have come by a combined seven points. Plus, Ohio State was still Ohio State when Indiana lost at home to the Buckeyes in October.

Everyone would rank the Hoosiers ahead of Iowa, Oregon, and USC in the Big Ten, which is exactly what the AP voters did this week.

The Longhorns dominated a 4-6 Arkansas team 45-3 on Saturday, and it was exponentially more impressive than Alabama's 47-0 win. It's incredible that sentence is factual, but it is, seeing as how Alabama's shutout came against FCS Chattanooga.

Derrek Cooper (5) of the Texas Longhorns is in action against the Arkansas Razorbacks at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, on Nov. 21, 2026. Texas defeated Arkansas 45-3. (Robert Backman/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)

FIFTH-RANKED TEXAS DOMINATES ARKANSAS AS ARCH MANNING IS HEATING UP AHEAD OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

Texas, Alabama, and Tennessee all sit at 9-2 on the season, and the Longhorns getting inside the Top 5 after UCLA and Indiana fell is inarguable. The Longhorns beat Tennessee earlier in the year, and the schedule broke with Alabama's cupcake game coming in the penultimate week of the season, hence the inside move on the Crimson Tide.

A week ago, the Longhorns were No. 8 while Alabama was a spot ahead.

The AP Poll is irrelevant due to the College Football Playoff Rankings ruling all, meaning the back end is even more pointless, but it gives college football fans something to argue about and argue we will.

Last week, voters elected to keep Ole Miss ranked at No. 25 after losing to Oklahoma. Florida was also ranked No. 23 a week ago. The Sooners beat both the Rebels and Gators earlier in the year, but did not have a number next to their name in Week 11.

Suddenly, a week too late, Oklahoma has surged to No. 19 ahead of the Gators and Rebels.

We can't just pick on the SEC teams when it comes to the back end of this week's poll, because what on Earth is Boise State doing at No. 22?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

San Diego State rushes the field after defeating Boise State 22-20 at Albertsons Stadium in Boise, Idaho, on Nov. 21, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

The Broncos lost 22-20 at home to what was a 5-5 San Diego State team on Saturday night for their second loss of the season.

Liberty, at No. 21, is the lone non-Power Four team that should be inside the Top 25, but we as a society decided long ago that 'the little guy' has to be shown preferential treatment, and internal fighting among voters may have broken out if only one Group of Five team had a number next to its name this late into the season.

Mark Harris is a writer for OutKick. Follow him on X @itismarkharris.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
articles.excerpt:
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the p...
articles.body_text:
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the pair kissing while surrounded by white roses.

Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, could be seen in the background of one image. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley.

Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said "I do" in a black suit from the same fashion house.

In one of the photographs, which was the first in a series of images shared by the singer in an Instagram post, the newly weds posed next to a golden retriever.

The post was captioned with "M+M" followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November.

Miley's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments.

The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra.

Guests stuck to an all-black dress code, according to reports.

'Angel by my side' - Miley Cyrus pays tribute to godmother Dolly Parton

Miley Cyrus confirms engagement to musician Maxx Morando

The American singer confirmed her engagement to the 28-year-old drummer during an interview with US TV show Good Morning America last year.

She said Morando had got down on one knee for the proposal during a trip to Asia.

"I am not easy to surprise because I love to control every situation and I had completely surrendered and I'm telling you, I was so, so, so surprised," she said.

During an interview with Wonderland, Morando said he "had to be really sneaky" to keep his proposal plans a secret.

"We went to Tokyo first for a couple days, and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could," he said.

Cyrus, 33, had previously been married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth but the couple separated in 2019.

The singer, whose hits include Party in the U.S.A and Wrecking Ball, married Hunger Games star Hemsworth in 2018 after the couple were in a relationship for a decade.

Speaking to British Vogue in 2023, Cyrus said she and 28-year-old Morando met after being "put on a blind date".

Morando is a drummer with LA-based band Liily. The band participated in NBC's Miley's New Year's Eve Party - hosted by Cyrus - in 2022, alongside musicians including Cyrus's late godmother Dolly Parton and David Byrne.

articles.title: DK Metcalf disqualified from Steelers game for unsportsmanlike penalties including poking opponent's facemask
articles.excerpt:

DK Metc...
articles.body_text:
"So, I get the rule and what the wording in the rule is. But these angles change so quickly in fractions of a second, right at the right at the time of contact that it's kind of it's unfair."

DK Metcalf is clearly frustrated about this season because he's not producing as expected and on Sunday we saw what could be a full manifestation of that frustration when he was disqualified from the game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The incident happened in chapters on consecutive Steelers' drives and culminated with 4:58 left in the third quarter when Metcalf seemed to poke the facemask of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

DK METCALF WILL NOT FACE CRIMINAL CHARGES FOR VIRAL ALTERCATION WITH LIONS FANS

This fracas was away from the play and even after the play was over. But officials caught it, and disqualified Metcalf for picking up his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the third quarter.

Officials called Metcalf for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty because, they said, he was taunting DeJean. The Eagles contend Metcalf poked DeJean in the facemask.

The previous possession by the Steelers offense, Metcalf had gotten into a kerfuffle with DeJean and been flagged for his first unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

Pittsburgh Steelers' DK Metcalf walks off the field after an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan, on Dec. 21, 2025. (Ryan Sun/AP Photo)

We have no idea what led to this little brouhaha between Metcalf and DeJean. On the first play, Metcalf turned a block of DeJean into a push, during which he grabbed DeJean by his neck and then the front of his collar.

DeJean (6-foot and 198 pounds) then grabbed the bigger Metcalf (6-4 and 235) around his collar and the two men started pushing on each other.

But Metcalf was apparently very hot because he could be seen jawing at DeJean even as other Eagles and, eventually, Steelers players joined the fray.

(By the way, NFL moments like this are a sportswriter's dream because they allow for the use of words such as kerfuffle, brouhaha and fracas).

Pittsburgh Steelers' DK Metcalf wipes his face on the bench during the second half of an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions, Sunday, Dec. 21, 2025, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Rey Del Rio)

Anyway, as the two men were locked onto each other's collars, officials joined the tussle and pulled each player away.

Except that when the game umpire stood between Metcalf and his ability to rejoin the rumpus, he put a hand on Metcalf's chest.

And Metcalf swiped it away – which is surely about to get the NFL's attention beyond the disqualification.

Anyway, Metcalf was penalized for unnecessary roughness as his first offense.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

So Metcalf went to the locker room with more personal foul penalties (2) than catches (1), and he cost the Steelers more yards by penalty (19) than the yards he contributed via his catch (1).

Pittsburgh Steelers' DK Metcalf, right, plays against Detroit Lions' Rock Ya-Sin during the second half of an NFL football game, Sunday, Dec. 21, 2025, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Ryan Sun)

NFL SUSPENDS BUFFALO BILLS SAFETY CJ GARDNER-JOHNSON AFTER GROTESQUE SPITTING INCIDENT

Metcalf is supposed to be Pittsburgh's top receiver but had only 35 catches for 432 yards and 2 TDs in nine games coming into Sunday's action.

One more thing: Metcalf has something of a history as a hothead.

During the 2025 NFL season, Metcalf was suspended for two games without pay by the NFL for initiating a physical confrontation with a fan during a Week 16 game at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions on December 21, 2025.

articles.title: TCU fires Sonny Dykes after giving him a spring extension, and fans' reactions say it all
articles.excerpt:
Seven months after handing Sonny Dykes a massive extension, the powers at TCU decided they'd seen enough.

The program let go of the TCU football head coach Sunday, a day after the 38-17 dismantling b...
articles.body_text:
Seven months after handing Sonny Dykes a massive extension, the powers at TCU decided they'd seen enough.

The program let go of the TCU football head coach Sunday, a day after the 38-17 dismantling by the second-ranked Utah Utes.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Athletic Director Mike Buddie issued the school's statement, nodding to the 2022 run before laying out the slide since.

Saturday marked TCU's final home game of the season.

"Since 2022, however, the Frogs have posted a 28-21 overall record and a 17-18 mark in the Big 12 while finishing or ranking 10th or worst in penalty yards per game within the league each of the past four seasons," the statement read, in part.

TCU head coach Sonny Dykes walks the field before a game against Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas, on Nov. 21, 2026. (Getty Images)

Texas Christian University Horned Frogs head coach Sonny Dykes reacts to a call during the second half against the BYU Cougars at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo, Utah, on Nov. 15, 2025. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

"After appearing in the Big 12 Championship Game in 2022, TCU has finished an average of 7th in the league standings since. With Saturday's result, the Frogs currently sit in 12th."

"While Sonny's tenure began with the incredible achievement of winning the 2022 Fiesta Bowl and advancing to the national championship game, the proceeding years have seen our program slide further away from that mountain top than can be accepted," Buddie said.

"I am grateful to Sonny for his belief in TCU, his family's love for the Fort Worth community, and for his coaching staff's commitment to recruiting and developing men of high character."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT

"TCU's investment in football has led to dramatic growth of our university and city in the past 20 years, and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return, especially at such a pivotal time of change in college sports.

"We expect to compete for Big 12 championships, to be a central figure in the College Football Playoff conversation, and our continued investment and growth potential reflects that. I expect our new leader will echo those sentiments, rally our fan base behind that challenge, and put a team on the field that our alumni, fans, students, and community will be excited to support."

Sonny Dykes of Texas Christian University stands on the sidelines during the second half at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, Ariz., on Nov. 6, 2026. (Getty Images)

Dykes’s five-year stint in Fort Worth opened with a 12-0 regular season behind Max Duggan and a 51-45 Fiesta Bowl upset of Michigan; then the carriage turned to a pumpkin in a 65-7 national championship loss to Georgia.

Despite posting 9-4 seasons in 2024 and 2025, a 5-7 slump in 2023 and a 5-6 mark in 2026 sealed his 41-23 tenure.

After his dismissal, TCU fans largely anticipated and accepted the move after a stretch of uneven seasons. Reactions on X happily capped the Dykes era.

Dublin, Ireland, on Aug. 29, 2026 — TCU head coach Sonny Dykes and North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick shake hands after the 2026 Aer Lingus College Football Classic at Aviva Stadium. (Sportsfile via Getty Images)

Some memes featured Dave Aranda and Brian Kelly (jokingly) as candidates for the vacancy, while one person suggested Shane Beamer, not so jokingly.

"He absolutely caught lightning in a bottle in 2022, and they’ll never reach that height again," one reaction read.

More poured in. "Couldn’t wait until after Thursday? Some of us need the Frogs locked in against Texas Tech."

Another reacted, "Kinda crazy TCU had the balls to do it."

Some took issue with TCU's decision-making on the extension's financials.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE

"They extended him in spring for no reason whatsoever. But paying players is what makes CFB broken."

OutKick Sr. college sports reporter Trey Wallace gave his first impressions, reading the tea leaves on TCU's next move.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"They are going to swing for the fences. Could USC head coach Lincoln Riley be interested if things continue trending in that direction in LA? Baylor is interested, so what about TCU? "

"A number of names will be interested because of how much TCU is willing to spend in hopes of contending in Big 12 and for CFP spot. They can attract hot names around the sport, and wouldn’t have fired Sonny Dykes if they didn’t already have a few names in mind."

FLORIDA STATE FIRES MIKE NORVELL AFTER FAN REVOLT, CLEMSON LOSS SPARK DECISION TO PAY MASSIVE BUYOUT

"They will owe him $20 million after giving him an extension in April," Trey noted.
