articles.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
articles.excerpt:
Wes Streeting told Volodymyr Zelensky he was in Kyiv to show that Europe was united in its support for Ukraine

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critic...
articles.body_text:
Wes Streeting told Volodymyr Zelensky he was in Kyiv to show that Europe was united in its support for Ukraine

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsular it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.

The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.

"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."

The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.

This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimean Bridge

Zelensky was speaking ahead of a meeting in Kyiv with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, who told the Ukrainian president he was here to show that Europe was united in its support.

"The more Putin tries to divide us, the more resolute we become," Streeting said.

He said that Russian missiles hitting Poland on Friday, during military exercises of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, was an "outrageous provocation".

The timing, Streeting said, seemed "more than a coincidence".

Asked by the BBC about Nato's response, he said the best way was to "do more for Ukraine" to defend itself against Putin who he called a "cold-blooded killer".

Streeting's visit to Kyiv came after European leaders meeting in Berlin on Thursday alongside US envoys said they were ready for negotiations with Moscow on ending the war in Ukraine.

"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president - who had also dialled into the meeting from Air Force One - wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side".

Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks - but earlier this week he invited European representatives to Moscow as it wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

That meeting in the German capital came hours after Putin had held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China, with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Zelensky said he had been "sceptical" ahead of the latest round of talks, when US envoys claimed that Russia was prepared to make compromises to end the war.

"I thought [Putin] would find reason to escalate."

Speaking to the BBC, Streeting added: "Putin has absolutely no business playing the victim. He is the aggressor in this war. He provoked an illegal invasion of Ukraine. And all of us, right throughout the world, need to judge Putin not on his words, but on his actions."

In a separate development on Saturday, Finland said it "detected a drone strike on a Russian merchant vessel" in the eastern Gulf of Finland, "in an international maritime area".

The Finnish defence ministry said in a statement that the vessel was damaged, without giving any further details.

It added that "temporary restrictions on aviation and maritime areas in the eastern Gulf of Finland" were now reinstated for safety reasons.

Russia has not publicly commented on the issue.

New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses

UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

articles.title: Russia says Kaliningrad-bound ship struck by drones in Gulf of Finland
articles.excerpt:
Two drones have struck a cargo ship bound for Russia’s exclave Kaliningrad in international waters of the Gulf of Finland, close to Russia’s maritime border, according to a senior Russian official.

T...
articles.body_text:
Two drones have struck a cargo ship bound for Russia’s exclave Kaliningrad in international waters of the Gulf of Finland, close to Russia’s maritime border, according to a senior Russian official.

The attack happened west of Gogland Island on Saturday morning, with Finland instating air and sea traffic restrictions in the eastern part of the gulf.

It is not clear who was behind the attack.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Russia’s Leningrad region, said the vessel’s crew were being evacuated and the damage had yet to be fully assessed.

“Three nautical miles from the Russian Federation’s border, a cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad was attacked by two drones,” he wrote on the messaging app Max.

Kaliningrad’s Governor Alexey Besprozvannykh said supplies to the Russian exclave were not at risk.

The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia, both NATO members. It connects Russia’s former capital of St Petersburg with its Kaliningrad enclave by sea.

Finland’s Ministry of Defence said its forces had detected a drone attack on a Russian vessel in international waters, with the vessel sustaining damage, and dispatched Finnish Border Guard units to the scene.

The ministry said air and sea traffic restrictions were a precaution in case further drones needed to be intercepted, adding that Finland had notified its allies of the incident.

“A Russian cargo ship is on fire in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The Finnish Border Guard is leading the maritime rescue operation and is preparing for potential environmental damage control within Finland’s area of responsibility,” Finland’s Border Guard said on its official website.

Ukraine and Russia have attacked each other’s shipping throughout the war, mostly in the Black Sea.

Earlier this month, Finland’s military said it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine took credit for. Helsinki said it had raised concerns about striking in the area with Kyiv afterwards.

Saturday’s attack has not been attributed to anyone.

articles.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
articles.excerpt: Security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during an attack on Ukraine on Friday. Poland’s government says it may have been hit by two missiles and a jet-...
articles.body_text:
Security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during an attack on Ukraine on Friday. Poland’s government says it may have been hit by two missiles and a jet-powered drone.

The incident, which took place as European troops held military drills in the country and as the United States pushes to revive talks on ending the war in Ukraine, have raised questions about whether the strike was deliberate.

So what happened, and does this mean Russia has struck Poland, a NATO member?

Poland’s Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference in Warsaw that two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory during Russia’s overnight attack on November 20. The missiles came down at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, while the jet-powered drone fell at Molodycz, all in the country’s southeast.

One missile is believed to have crashed about 35km (22 miles) from where European troops’ military exercises were taking place. A Kh-101 cruise missile went down about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and what officials believe was a jet-powered drone hit about 30km (20 miles) from the border. No immediate injuries or damage were reported.

That night, Russia launched one of its heaviest bombardments of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, some with cluster warheads. At least eight civilians were killed and more than two dozen were wounded.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it appeared “we are dealing with an intentional provocation” by Russia. He said the incident was likely timed to coincide with the European military exercises in Poland. The unprecedented two-week exercise began on November 9 in southeastern Poland and is preparing forces for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine to help stabilise the country and rebuild its military.

Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera that the incident “fits into a pattern going back for months” of Russia “testing how far they can go”.

“A few months ago, it was flying the drones into airspace, and indeed a couple of times they flew fighter jets across the border into the Baltic states,” he said. “You just test how NATO responds.”

This time, he said, Moscow had “gone a bit further”. “You lob a couple of missiles across and a drone” near where 11 countries are holding exercises.

The Polish Air Force had launched preventive air patrols on September 17 aimed at securing the eastern part of Polish airspace following repeated incursions in the previous weeks.

Harry Nedelcu, partner and senior director for geopolitics at Rasmussen Global, said the testing has not been limited to Poland.

“During the war, there’s been repeated instances of Russia testing NATO allies – Poland, Romania and also non-NATO Moldova as well, which is experiencing – especially over the last few months – increasing numbers of drones and missiles flying over its territory and airspace,” he told Al Jazeera.

He linked the incursions to one of Moscow’s core war aims. “One of the key goals in Ukraine that Russia has had in the full-scale invasion, that has lasted almost five years now, has been to prevent Ukraine from being a part of NATO,” he said. “So their goal clearly is to undermine NATO, to do everything possible to undermine it.

“What Russia is doing with these missiles, drones, that sometimes find their way into NATO territory, tests NATO just under the radar of Article 5 to see how far can they push things. How far can they take hybrid warfare?”

Under Article 5, each member of the NATO alliance understands that if one of them is the “victim of an armed attack, each and every other member of the alliance will consider this act of violence as an armed attack against all members”.

At a meeting on Thursday with European leaders in Germany’s capital, Berlin, US President Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said he believes Russia would be “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for post-war Ukraine.

Kushner and fellow special envoy Steve Witkoff have been holding talks with Ukraine and Russia in recent days, in a push for peace which has been viewed as sidelining Ukraine’s European allies.

Following the Berlin meeting, French President Emmanuel Macron said Ukraine’s membership of NATO should be considered again, prompting Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov to push back.

Ryabkov said any form of “quasi membership” for Kyiv of the Western ‌military alliance was totally unacceptable for Moscow, Russian state media reported.

Lucas said the timing of the missile incursion into Polish territory now is very likely tied to the ongoing US-led peace talks.

“The Russians cannot be seen to go through talks and completely exclude Europe,” he said. He described the Kremlin’s push for a “Europe-wide security architecture” as a way to avoid discussing a ceasefire or security guarantees for Ukraine.

“Rather than having a strong Europe at the talks, they want to try to divide Europe, they want to try to unsettle Europe, they want to try to scare Europe,” he said.

He also pointed to Ukraine’s recent strikes on the Kerch Bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia. He said these were seen as “a very serious attack on Russian capabilities” with “severe political, military and economic consequences”.

The latest Russian bombardment follows President Vladimir Putin’s pledge to retaliate against those strikes.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the missile incident a “grave violation” of Poland’s airspace. On X, he said the incident was “clearly dangerous” and a consequence of Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. Rutte is expected to visit Poland this weekend.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it “utterly unacceptable”. Germany’s Foreign Ministry called it “yet another example of Russia’s ongoing provocations”.

US President Donald Trump had played down earlier incursions hours before. “Putin has been landing drones in Poland and a couple of little missiles, by mistake,” he said.

Nedelcu said Warsaw’s reaction was “definitely a strong one”, with Polish officials “drawing a parallel between the fact that actually around the same time there were exercises by the Coalition of the Willing [those countries willing to provide support to Ukraine] nearby, and that this may have not been a coincidence”.

He said Poland is now “asking for more NATO support under this Eastern Sentry mission that already exists”.

“It’s not if, but what form that additional support will take – maybe an airborne early warning aircraft, or something of the sort,” he said.

“But what they have stopped short of is invoking Article 4,” he added, referring to the clause under which allies consult each other before invoking Article 5. “It’s unclear whether this was at their own volition. Maybe perhaps allies don’t want to use it too often, because Article 4 is also quite serious. It has been invoked not often, and it loses its value if it’s constantly invoked.”

Lucas said the public condemnation from European leaders was itself the message to Moscow. “It’s a signal to the Russians: look, we know what you’re doing, we see what you’re doing here,” he said.

“But you’re not going to run it up into an all-out military confrontation over a couple of missiles.”

He said he expects the response to be “defensive”, built on “preparedness” of ground forces, air, naval and cyber-defence, and defence against disinformation. “These will be the most intense preparations you will have had, certainly since the 1980s and possibly well before that,” he said.

On the same day, Denmark took action on a separate front. It announced that it was expelling Russia’s defence attache after Danish intelligence concluded that Moscow had orchestrated a plot to assassinate Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner during a concert near Copenhagen.

Probably not. Article 5 treats an attack on any ally as an attack on all 32 members, but invoking it is a political decision requiring agreement from all members, not an automatic trigger. Poland can instead invoke Article 4, which provides for emergency consultations only. Warsaw did so in September 2025, after Russian drones entered its airspace.

Lucas said NATO members want to stop Russia succeeding in Ukraine without allowing the conflict to escalate. “[That] means you set a very high bar for invoking Article 5,” he said.

“You’re talking about what in effect would be a sustained Russian attack on Poland. That’s when Article 5 gets invoked.”

He said NATO is also handling a delicate diplomatic moment. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are pressing for a negotiated settlement, and “NATO can’t be seen to be the ones to sabotage the talks”.

Those talks remain murky, particularly after Kushner’s comments indicating that Russia would be “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for post-war Ukraine.

“Jared Kushner is going around making statements that make absolutely no sense about what deal is on the table,” Lucas said. He said the US is “so desperate for a deal” that it is “muddying the waters”.

Lucas said Ukraine has no real prospect of NATO membership now, because “bringing Ukraine into NATO would destabilise a ceasefire”. He said the goal should be “security guarantees as if Ukraine was a NATO member”.

Analysts say a direct confrontation between Russia and NATO is unlikely for now.

“The alliance shows every signal that it does not want to show any teeth,” Nedelcu said. “So what will probably happen, Russia will keep on testing the alliance. We should not expect that this is the last instance of this.

“The alliance is not trying to show Russia, you know, enough is enough, so Russia will still keep testing because they want to see where that threshold is,” he said.

Lucas said the bigger danger is a wider campaign of hybrid, or “grey zone”, warfare, including cyberattacks and disinformation, rather than direct strikes. “That’s where the real threat here is right now, rather than direct Russian strikes,” he said.

“I’m not going to say that it couldn’t escalate at some point, because you always have unintended escalation,” he added. “But I don’t want to go to the headlines and say this is it, World War III.”

Inside Ukraine, Nedelcu said, the war is intensifying in the air rather than on the ground. He described the incident in Poland as “a residual, if you will, collateral of the conflict in Ukraine”.

“On the front line, the conflict in Ukraine is pretty much static,” he said. “But what happens in Ukraine is that the air attack has been increasingly amplified, I would say, since the end of the summer.

“Russia is trying to essentially make Ukrainian cities especially unliveable – destroying its energy grid, trying to undermine even water supply, bridges, railways, logistics – in order to, if they cannot break it on the front lines, break it economically and break its civilian population.”

Lucas said any offensive pressure on Moscow would come through Ukraine’s own counterattacks, which he said Europe and NATO back, but the Trump administration does not.

“The more that you limit Russia’s capacity by hitting its refineries, its chemical plants, its engineering plants, by hitting the bridges, the more you increase the pressure on the Russians to try to stop the invasion,” he said.

articles.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled
articles.excerpt:
Iranian forces say they have shot down two US drones over the Strait of Hormuz, as the United States steps up its economic pressure campaign against Iran.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)...
articles.body_text:
Iranian forces say they have shot down two US drones over the Strait of Hormuz, as the United States steps up its economic pressure campaign against Iran.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday a new air defence system had intercepted and shot down an MQ-9 drone, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB. It said the incident marked the 58th such drone brought down by Iranian forces since the start of the war nearly nine months ago.

Later on Saturday, the IRGC also claimed bringing down an MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the 19th such downing.

There was no immediate comment by the US military.

The incidents come days after the US and Iran engaged in direct, tit-for-tat strikes, against a backdrop of increasing Iranian attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway through which one-fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed in peacetime.

Launched by the US and Israel on February 28, the war has killed thousands of people and severely disrupted shipping, pushing global energy prices higher and spreading to countries across the region.

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June, but it was never fully implemented because of disagreements over freedom and security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with attacks resuming periodically since July. In August, The Washington Post reported that the US had lost 45 MQ-9 drones, or about 25 percent of its fleet at a cost of more than $1.3bn, during combat operations in Iran.

As an agreement to end the war remains elusive, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday outlined his country’s positions on negotiations with the US, citing a seven-day proposal delivered to the US in September.

In an interview with state media, Araghchi said the seven conditions Iran has put forward “must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen”. The conditions include ending the war and lifting sanctions and the naval blockade on Iran’s southern ports.

Araghchi said Iran was prepared to negotiate how the conditions should be implemented, saying its timetable was “flexible”. The negotiations would be “conditional on the American side taking necessary confidence-building measures”, he added.

The top diplomat also ruled out Iran transferring its stockpile of 60 percent enriched uranium abroad, but said a “fair solution” could be reached and a number of proposals by mediators were “worth examining”.

Araghchi said that the current “no war, no peace” state of the conflict was undesirable, but that Iran could not accept an agreement that would “hand victory to the other side”.

At a Friday news conference at the White House, US President Donald Trump told reporters that Tehran “want to make a deal” but not one that is acceptable to him.

“We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they’ve been doing for 51 years,” alleged Trump, who had said last week that a deal with Iran on ending the war was unnecessary.

At the same news conference, US Vice President JD Vance, who had previously blamed the war for Republicans losing both chambers of Congress earlier this month, declined to say whether he would have authorised strikes on Iran to prevent the country from developing a nuclear weapon.

Vance said the decision to attack Iran in February was Trump’s call, “and my job is to support the president of the United States.”

⁠Separately on Friday, the US Treasury ⁠⁠said it had imposed sanctions on four Iranians it said acted as “oil trustees”, collecting money from ⁠⁠illicit international oil sales for Iran to evade sanctions and the US naval blockade on its southern ports.

The Treasury said in a statement that ⁠⁠in many cases the trustees have kept oil revenues for personal gain. Among the individuals sanctioned are Mohammad Javad Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, and Majid Taj, brother of ‌‌the Iranian Football Federation’s President Mehdi Taj, the Treasury said.

The new sanctions put ⁠⁠the individuals on the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control’s Specially Designated Nationals list, freezing any assets they may have under US jurisdiction and effectively prohibiting dollar ⁠⁠transactions with them or entities that they control.

The Treasury also said it imposed sanctions ⁠⁠on Mohammad Hossein Servati, the son of IRGC ⁠⁠Brigadier General Mohsen Servati, who has held positions in companies that brokered and received shipments of Iranian oil for delivery to independent Chinese “teapot” refineries.

Another sanctioned individual is ‌‌Mojtaba Arabnejad, the son of the sanctioned Mahan Air CEO Hamid Arabnejad. The Treasury said that Mojtaba Arabnejad has purchased aircraft ‌‌parts ‌‌for the sanctioned Mahan Air and overseen oil sales that have partly supported the airline.

Meanwhile, as Republicans grapple with the fallout from the sweeping midterm election losses, Democratic Representatives Yassamin Ansari and Ro Khanna called on Congress to use an upcoming government funding bill to end spending for offensive military operations against Iran.

Citing the mounting costs of the war, they issued a video statement urging fellow legislators to reject any funding package that keeps paying for the war, with a deadline looming next month to adopt a budget.

Failing to pass a spending bill by December 11 could trigger a government shutdown, a risk that has made some Democrats wary of drawing a red line on the war on Iran.

Rosa DeLauro and Patty Murray, the top Democrats responsible for appropriations, have said they would prefer to find ways to end the war without risking a government shutdown.

articles.title: Inside the 'Lion’s Den': Real estate brothers bragged about 'hunting' women before 30-year prison terms
articles.excerpt:
Attorney Michael Willemin says private jets, superyachts and powerful connections helped the convicted brothers operate for years and left women fearful of coming forward.

The Alexander brothers sold...
articles.body_text:
Attorney Michael Willemin says private jets, superyachts and powerful connections helped the convicted brothers operate for years and left women fearful of coming forward.

The Alexander brothers sold multimillion-dollar mansions, mingled with the wealthy and lived like real estate golden boys. But behind the luxury and excess, prosecutors said, was a decades-long pattern of sexual abuse.

In text messages presented at trial and featured in a new docuseries, the brothers and their associates discussed "hunting" for women. "We are running out of prey," Oren wrote in one message.

Convicted of federal sex trafficking offenses and each sentenced to 30 years in prison, Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander are the subjects of a new Peacock true crime docuseries, "The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers," which features accounts from women who say the trio sexually assaulted them.

ALEXANDER BROTHERS ALLEGEDLY PAID FOR COVERAGE OF SEX-TRAFFICKING TRIAL AS WRITERS DENY FAVORABLE TREATMENT

Oren Alexander (center) and his twin brother, Alon (right) attend their bond hearing at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Friday, Dec. 13, 2024, in Miami, Florida. Alon, Oren, and Tal Alexander were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison on Oct. 27, 2026. (Matias J. Ocner/Pool via REUTERS)

"The brothers at trial, they said, 'We're not predators, we were just playboys,’" director Emma Schwartz told Fox News Digital. "But at the same time, you see their own words. Oren says he would hunt women like he hunts a client. And that's not exactly language about seducing people. The word 'hunt' was used a lot in their messages."

"The prosecutor's theory to the jury, and the public, was that these men invited women out to the Hamptons, women who traveled through New York, and the whole purpose was to sexually assault or rape them," Schwartz said. "There were messages like, 'Let's orgy them out,' with a clear intent that sex was involved."

Prosecutor Madison Smyser questions Katie Moore (pseudonym) during the federal sex trafficking trial of high-profile real estate agent brothers Tal Alexander, Alon Alexander and Oren Alexander, sitting before Judge Valerie E. Caproni, in New York City, on Jan. 27 2026, in a courtroom sketch. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)

The Alexander brothers, born into wealth, grew up to be real estate golden boys. Oren and Tal, former star brokers at Douglas Elliman, later co-founded their own real estate firm specializing in luxury properties in Miami, New York City and Los Angeles. The brothers were involved in high-profile real estate transactions, including a nearly $240 million penthouse sale in 2019 that set a record for the most expensive residential sale in U.S. history. They co-founded the luxury real estate firm Official in 2022.

Defense attorney Teny Geragos speaks near Oren Alexander at the start of the federal sex trafficking trial of high-profile real estate agent brothers Tal Alexander, Alon Alexander and Oren Alexander in New York City, on Jan. 27, 2026, in a courtroom sketch. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)

Alon was an executive at his family's private security company.

Together, they moved in elite circles and hosted lavish parties in Miami, New York City, the Hamptons and Aspen. Court filings previously obtained by Fox News Digital alleged that the brothers used "the promise of luxury experiences, travel and accommodations" to lure women to locations where they were then sexually assaulted.

Oren Alexander and Tal Alexander speak at a panel at the Rockstars of Real Estate Event on Sept. 3, 2013, in New York City. (Amy Sussman/Invision for DETAILS Magazine/AP Images, File)

According to the docuseries, the brothers exchanged messages in secret group chats, including one message that read, "Welcome to the Lion's Den." The conversations included discussions about "hunting" for women and what the participants expected in return.

Brothers Oren, Alon, and Tal Alexander at an exclusive VIP venue. Prosecutors say they used their glamorous lifestyle of luxury travel and nightclubs as a hunting ground to drug and sexually assault women, leading to their 2026 conviction and 30-year prison sentences. (Peacock)

"All content in this chat stays in the chat," one text shown in the film warned.

In another text shown in the film, Oren said "boys need to hunt" because "we are running out of prey." He appeared to write, "Met a cute Canadian and took her back to the crib and trained her." When one person texted, "No is not an option," Oren replied, "Nope."

Tal Alexander and Oren Alexander are seen here on a yacht, circa 2013. (Photo by Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

In a separate group chat, Oren warned that the "boys are hungry," while Tal wrote, "Girls look fresh," according to court documents.

Real estate titans Oren and Tal Alexander, along with their brother Alon, enjoyed a lifestyle of private jets, superyachts and A-list VIP access that made them fixtures of the New York and Miami social scenes. (Peacock)

Prosecutors later alleged in a court filing that the brothers raped or sexually assaulted at least 70 women, describing them as "serial rapists." Several women described receiving gifts and being flown to luxury destinations where they said they were given drugs before being assaulted.

"The only thing can bring us down is some h-- complaining," one text attributed to Oren read in the film.

According to the federal indictment, the brothers sometimes used existing social connections or the guise of starting a genuine romantic relationship to lure women into meeting them privately. (Peacock)

"I think the most surprising thing was some of the messages that came out, things that they put in writing themselves as the way they and their friends talked about women," Schwartz said.

The Alexander brothers are being held in New York City at the Metropolitan Detention Center (MDC) in Brooklyn. (Peacock)

"Often, it was very uncomfortable and hard to hear. They used language like they want to get 'the best ROI' on bringing women on a trip, as if women are property or something to get a return on investment. There's also a blog post where their friends had outlined a certain psychology about why they get pleasure out of hurting women. Those messages got into a sense of how they thought about things."

"People can say that they've never done that," Schwartz said. "But when you see over and over things in writing that speak to not believing in consent, it's a lot easier to believe when a woman gets up there and testifies about what happened."

Federal prosecutors and court filings state that dozens of women came forward with allegations of sexual assault against the Alexander brothers. (Peacock)

Prosecutors said the brothers' alleged sexual abuse dated back more than two decades, to their high school years in Miami. For the docuseries, Schwartz interviewed several former students who attended the same high school as the brothers or knew them personally.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The Alexander brothers are pictured during their high school years in Miami, where prosecutors and accusers say their pattern of predatory behavior and unchecked entitlement first began years before their 2026 sex-trafficking conviction. (Peacock)

"There was more than one person who said, 'I'm not entirely surprised by the allegations that came out,'" Schwartz said. "They had felt there had been similar, or in the beginning, patterns that one might see later on."

"These cases can be really difficult, especially when you have teenagers who may not always tell their own story straight because they don't want to admit what they did or that they snuck out and something happened," she said.

Alon, Oren, and Tal Alexander were deeply intertwined personally, professionally, and throughout the crimes for which they were convicted. Born roughly a year apart — with Alon and Oren as twins and Tal as the eldest — the trio operated as a tightly-knit unit across virtually every aspect of their lives. (Peacock)

"I think there's always questions about what lessons someone could have learned, and those were questions that some of the people who went to high school with them still had."

The Alexander Brothers hosted lavish parties across Miami, New York and the Hamptons that prosecutors say they used to lure and assault women. (Peacock)

"There were allegations that went back a very long time," Schwartz added.

The brothers' downfall began in June 2024, when two civil lawsuits accusing Oren and Alon of sexual assault became public. As more women came forward with similar allegations, the FBI investigated accusations of sexual violence spanning more than a decade.

Oren Alexander poses for a jail booking photograph after his arrest in Miami, Florida, on Dec. 11, 2024. (via REUTERS)

On Dec. 11, 2024, all three brothers were arrested in Miami on federal sex trafficking charges. Prosecutors accused the trio of using their wealth and status to lure women to lavish parties, luxury properties and exclusive trips, where prosecutors said the women were drugged and sexually assaulted.

Damian Williams, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, announces the arrest and indictment of Alon Alexander, Oren Alexander, and Tal Alexander, on charges of sex trafficking and drugs, at 26 Federal Plaza in New York City, on Dec. 11, 2024. (REUTERS/Kent Edwards)

During their six-week trial, 11 women testified against the brothers, including several who said they were minors at the time of the encounters. Lindsey Acree, an artist and gallery owner, testified that she was raped by Tal and another man at a Hamptons home in 2011 after taking a drink that she said left her feeling paralyzed.

"The biggest thing is why? Why did you do this?" Acree asked. "I don’t understand the cruelty. I don’t understand the hatred toward women."

Alon Alexander poses for a jail booking photograph after his arrest in Miami, Florida, on Dec. 11, 2024. (via REUTERS)

Another woman who said Tal raped her in August 2014 told the court she carried "a quiet funeral in me for the person I might have become had this not happened to me."

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Prosecutor Madison Smyser points towards high-profile real estate agent brothers Tal Alexander, Alon Alexander and Oren Alexander, sitting before Judge Valerie E. Caproni, during her opening statement at the start of their federal sex trafficking trial in New York City, on Jan. 27, 2026, in a courtroom sketch. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)

"Every second that Tal raped me in that shower felt like an eternity of terror," the woman, who used a pseudonym, said.

Another woman, describing her rape at a Hamptons mansion, said, "What looked like a beautiful place became for me a mansion of horror, a mansion of dark secrets."

Tal Alexander poses for an identification portrait in an undated photograph. (via REUTERS)

Lexi Zettle said Tal was once "a prince in my eyes" who offered her the promise of a "fairytale" romance before he began pressuring her to have sex with his business associates.

GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB

Real estate brokers Tal Alexander (right) and his younger brother, Oren Alexander, outside their Miami Beach home on Friday, Feb. 1, 2019. (Getty Images)

"They treated me like a rag doll, like I was this disposable thing," Zettle said.

Oren Alexander, Tal Alexander and Alon Alexander attend the Chanukah With the Stars Gala on Dec. 10, 2014, at Harmonie Club in New York City. (Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

On March 9, 2026, a federal jury in New York City found the brothers guilty. All three were convicted of multiple federal sex offenses, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking. On Oct. 27, they were each sentenced to 30 years in prison. U.S. District Judge Valerie E. Caproni told them, "Your conduct was monstrous," equating them to Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

Alon Alexander (right) and his twin brother, Oren (left) attend their bond hearing at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Dec. 13, 2024, in Miami, Florida. (Getty Images)

The brothers argued that becoming husbands and fathers had changed them from their womanizing ways. While none of them testified at trial, each spoke before their sentencing. Oren said he and his brothers came of age at the height of hookup culture and regretted many of the things he said about women. Still, he insisted they had never broken the law.

A tearful Tal said, "I feel like an atomic bomb has been dropped on my life and destroyed everything in its wake." Alon said he had built a different life since his partying years.

All three brothers have consistently denied the criminal allegations against them. (Peacock)

"Thirty years is a very long sentence," Schwartz said. "They'll be almost 70. Each of them has children and will essentially miss their entire childhood."

Real estate brokers Oren and Tal Alexander and their brother Alon, who were found guilty of repeatedly drugging, sexually assaulting, and raping dozens of female victims, listen as their lawyers argue for a lesser sentence on their behalf in a New York courtroom on Oct. 27, 2026, in this courtroom sketch. (REUTERS)

Schwartz hopes the docuseries will challenge common misconceptions about sex trafficking and shed light on how victims can be exploited.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Following the brothers' conviction and sentencing, their defense attorneys announced plans to appeal the verdicts. (Peacock)

In response to the documentary producers' questions, Tal denied pressuring Zettle to have sex with potential clients. Oren denied sexually assaulting Acree and said she continued to socialize with him. All three brothers denied drugging or sexually assaulting anyone and said they planned to appeal their convictions.

"The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers" is available for streaming. (Peacock)

Fox News Digital’s Greg Wehner and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Tech outages give broadcast media just another opportunity to bash Republicans
articles.excerpt:
"The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded Democrats work to impeach Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. next year.

Whenever anything goes wrong in America, the ...
articles.body_text:
"The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg demanded Democrats work to impeach Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. next year.

Whenever anything goes wrong in America, the broadcast networks have a reflex to suggest things must have gone awry because the Trump administration is so remarkably incompetent and unqualified to govern anything.

It began last weekend when a nationwide ground stop underlined a problem with the nation’s air traffic control system, which still used floppy disks. On the Sunday shows, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy received the same antagonistic routine from the broadcast hosts: Why haven’t you done anything about this?

At every stop, Duffy explained that the Trump administration has been trying to get funding for a revamp, but Congress was very specific in how it appropriated funds. Duffy had an answer, but Trump had to be blamed. Don’t try suggesting that the Obama and Biden administrations passed massive infrastructure bills and somehow didn’t get this job done. The New York Post reported Biden’s Transportation Department under Secretary Pete Buttigieg spent $80 billion on DEI programs. The networks weren’t going to be outraged or offended at the contrast.

DUFFY VOWS TO MODERNIZE AGING AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

On the left-wing late-night comedy shows, the networks made fun of Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin as unqualified. On NBC’s "Tonight Show," Jimmy Fallon interviewed Duffy and Mullin impersonators. "I'm not sure you guys are inspiring a lot of confidence from the American people."

Whoopi Goldberg on "The View" (Screenshot/ABC)

Fake Duffy replied, "Look, I'm a former ‘Real World’-‘Road Rules’ reality TV contestant who's wearing this stupid little jacket like I'm Airplane Ken." Fake Mullin added, "And I'm a former UFC fighter who's been hit in the head so many times, my brain issued a nationwide ground stop for my thoughts."

DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE'

ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel – who sampled two different colleges for one year after high school and never returned or graduated – pulled the same routine. "We learned, this weekend, a very valuable lesson. We learned what happens when the only experience your secretary of Transportation has when it comes to transportation is being on ‘Road Rules: All Stars’ on MTV." Later, he added: "Fortunately, they have got some of the top minds working on this, like plumber-turned head of Homeland Security, the router-rooter Markwayne Mullin." They pretend these men didn’t serve in the House and Senate, like they were plucked off the street.

The tech incidents piled up during the week. Several banks had problems. Many Microsoft users were locked out of their email systems, crippling their offices. Apple users said Tuesday morning they were unable to use the App Store, Apple Pay and other services. At the National Security Agency outside Washington, an internal communications network went down. The agency announced this happened during scheduled routine maintenance.

MICROSOFT’S MASSIVE OUTAGE OFFERS A LESSON IN HOW TO BRING THE WORLD BACK ONLINE

All of these things made Americans wonder about what could go wrong. Then people start talking about stocking up on food and water and generators like some catastrophe is in the offing.

Speaking of unqualified comedians, Whoopi Goldberg came on "The View" with more of her crackpot conspiracy theories. All this was happening right after the Democrats won big. "I just find it interesting that all of these things that have been put in place, suddenly, suddenly now, two weeks after a blue wave, everything's going wrong. Everything is kind of weird. Call me paranoid." She blamed Elon Musk: "But the man in charge of DOGE has a lot of stuff in the air and he seems to have control over a lot of things that go on around the world. It just - It makes me uncomfortable." She repeated her blue-wave conspiracies as the week went on.

MAMDANI TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S RESPONSE TO TECH OUTAGES: 'FAR FROM WHAT MANY WANTED TO HEAR'

Kimmel even made fun of the argument that the temporary ground stop wasn’t deadly. He played a clip of Texas Republican Rep. Michael McCaul at a hearing telling Mullin: "I'm going to start with you, Mr. Secretary. First of all, let me commend you, 36,000 planes being grounded. Yes, it was chaotic. But you know what, nobody died." Kimmel reacted by laughing as if McCaul was giving Mullin credit for clearing the lowest of low bars, "Nobody died? Of course nobody died. None of the planes were able to take off."

This marks the way "holding the government accountable" works at the networks. When something goes wrong with a Democrat president in power, the journalistic assumption is that you can’t blame the Democrats. Things just happened. Let’s not connect any dots. It’s the absolute opposite with Republicans. You can connect dots that don’t make a straight line. Democrats are presumed to be competent and well-educated. Republicans are cartooned as not very bright.

You could argue that the Republican response to these outages did not inspire confidence. But part of that confidence mission is based on network TV stars badgering them as The Problem. This partisan media system is especially frustrating when people are honestly scared. This isn’t just a routine fight over taxes and spending. It’s about people feeling unsafe as technology gets more complex. No one expects this "mainstream" media to calm things down when people feeling unsettled might accrue to their benefit.

articles.title: 'Bratty men' demand 'prince treatment' in dating trend, sparking debate over who should pay
articles.excerpt:
‘Fox & Friends’ discusses a debate over men demanding ‘princess treatment’ from their partners in relationships.

Some men are demanding "prince treatment" in the dating world, according to a dating t...
articles.body_text:
‘Fox & Friends’ discusses a debate over men demanding ‘princess treatment’ from their partners in relationships.

Some men are demanding "prince treatment" in the dating world, according to a dating trend making headlines, with men expecting women to pay for meals and spoil them.

Cosmopolitan magazine relationships writer Syeda Khaula Saad dubbed men with these expectations "bratty men," in a piece published in early November.

VICE, meanwhile, reported that the debate over "who's supposed to spoil whom" has gotten out of hand.

CHELSEA HANDLER SAYS ‘SOMETHING’S WRONG’ WITH MEN AS SHE RIPS MODERN DATING CULTURE

According to the publications, "bratty men" are turning the concept of "princess treatment" on its head.

Some men are demanding "prince treatment," expecting women to pay for dates and shower them with attention, according to recent reports. (Getty Images/IStock)

Men who want "prince treatment" expect pampering, extra attention and gifts. The trend is a reversal of "princess treatment," the notion that women should be spoiled with flowers, love notes, and other romantic gestures.

MAN TRIGGERS RELATIONSHIP CRISIS BY GRABBING FIRST CLASS, LEAVING WOMAN BEHIND IN COACH

"I’ve seen countless women sharing their experiences with what I’m now calling 'bratty men.' They’re demanding to have their meals paid for, that women drive them around, and whatever this is," Saad wrote Nov. 9. "They’re announcing that they’re 'the prize' and that a woman, or a date, should be spoiling them."

Toronto publication Now Toronto asked residents to weigh in on the "prince treatment" trend, highlighting a video by Toronto-based TikTok creator Shaurya Manocha arguing that men deserve to be spoiled.

'THE VOW' HOST CHRIS HARRISON SAYS YOUNG PEOPLE ARE DITCHING DATING APPS, TURNING TO CHURCH

Dave Portnoy, founder of Barstool Sports, discounted reports of "bratty men," arguing he didn't know any women who would put up with that treatment on the dating scene. (iStock/Getty Images)

"I would want my daughter to have somebody treat her like the princess that she is… I take care of her, I cherish her — same thing with my wife," a father and husband told Now Toronto.

Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy was asked about the "bratty men" trend during an interview with Fox Business host Stuart Varney on Wednesday.

'LOOKSMAXXING' INFLUENCER CLAVICULAR REJECTS INCEL LABEL, FAULTS 'BOTH' MEN AND WOMEN

Portnoy said he wasn't sure how much of the trend he believed, asking, "What type of woman would ever want this, or go out with this?"

"This seems a made-up thing," he added. "I haven't seen anywhere in my travels that women are willingly or wanting to pick up the check and pick up after and be treated like garbage. So I hope this trend isn't real."

WHY EVERYTHING YOUR SPOUSE SAYS IRRITATES YOU — AND WHAT IT COULD MEAN FOR YOUR MARRIAGE

Susan Trombetti, matchmaker and CEO of Exclusive Matchmaking, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "The bratty men and bratty women are out there. It's a competition of the brats and a response to the women who expect the guy's first-class upgrade."

Dating experts said there is nothing wrong with either men or women wanting special treatment on dates but said that this treatment should be reciprocated. (iStock/Getty Images)

"All the social media influencers and podcasters are trying to up the ante to get subscribers and promote this idea that men should be the ones on the pedestal. Your normal, nice guy that can't get a date or find someone is vulnerable to this sort of nonsense. They figure, 'Why not give it a try?' Women are demanding Ubers and gifts on dates, so why can't they sit back and demand, too? The problem is that neither the men nor the women who do this are high-value partners," Trombetti added.

MEN ARE SKIPPING SHOWERS BEFORE DATES FOR A REASON THAT MAY SURPRISE WOMEN

She called the idea "ridiculous" and said healthy relationships require give-and-take. Trombetti also said the "bratty men" trend likely wasn't too prevalent.

"I think it's more of a social media narrative where influencers try to get the most views and go viral," she said.

Relationship expert April Davis, founder of Luma Luxury Matchmaking, told Fox News Digital: "A man wanting to be taken out to dinner once in a while isn’t the problem. Why wouldn’t he want that? The question is whether he does thoughtful things for you too or if you’re the one always taking care of him."

Matchmaking experts weighed in on the idea that men are demanding "prince treatment" from women in the dating scene. (iStock/Getty Images)

"If you want a man who plans dates and picks up the check, you can look for that. If he wants someone who takes turns, that’s fine, too. You may just not be right for each other. There’s no need to turn it into a fight about what all men or all women should do," Davis added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

A debate over "princess treatment" spread across social media in July 2025 after a video went viral of a woman explaining what her husband does when the two of them go to a restaurant together.

"If I am at a restaurant with my husband, I do not talk to the hostess, I do not open any doors and I do not order my own food," the woman said in the video, according to The New York Times.

Some women reacting to the video called it "regressive," according to the Times. A 26-year-old grad student told the outlet at the time, that "princess treatment" can look "however you want it to look."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Biotech CEO says the US is fighting fentanyl ‘all wrong,’ urges new Democratic Congress to step up
articles.excerpt:
ARMR Sciences CEO Collin Gage tells Fox News Digital how a preventative bloodstream countermeasure designed for battlefield bioterror threats could protect troops and everyday Americans.

WASHINGTON —...
articles.body_text:
ARMR Sciences CEO Collin Gage tells Fox News Digital how a preventative bloodstream countermeasure designed for battlefield bioterror threats could protect troops and everyday Americans.

WASHINGTON — America is approaching the fentanyl crisis "all wrong" by waiting to reverse overdoses after they begin instead of blocking the drug with an experimental fentanyl vaccine, ARMR Sciences CEO Collin Gage told Fox News Digital.

In an exclusive interview, Gage urged the new incoming Democrat-controlled Congress to build on President Donald Trump's designation of illicit fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction and treat emerging synthetic drugs as a biodefense priority. ‘SUPER-DRUG’ 10 TIMES STRONGER THAN FENTANYL LINKED TO DEATHS ACROSS MULTIPLE STATES

"If you look at the overdose crisis like any other health crisis, really as a disease, you'll know the best way to treat a crisis is by preventing it altogether," Gage said. "We need to completely overhaul the treatment paradigm and focus on preventing these deaths with new innovative therapeutics, rather than continuing the same approach that historically has led to tens of thousands of deaths, hundreds of thousands of deaths over the last several years."

President Donald Trump signed an executive order classifying fentanyl as a "weapon of mass destruction" during a ceremony in the Oval Office on Dec. 15, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers discovered more than 16 pounds of fentanyl hidden inside an electric moped during a secondary inspection, authorities said. (U.S. Customs and Border Protection)

Fentanyl pills seized by the DEA in New Mexico on April 28, 2025. New Mexico officials have since launched a criminal investigation into allegations involving the agency's handling of separate fentanyl shipments. (DEA via AP)

Photo released by the DEA shows fentanyl pills seized in New Mexico on April 28, 2025, as the agency faces scrutiny over allegations it allowed other shipments to reach the streets. (DEA via AP)

Gage pointed to President Donald Trump's designation of illicit fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction as "absolutely critical" to shifting Washington toward a biodefense strategy.

Gage says emerging synthetic drugs pose a distinct biological threat, unlike traditional chemical or biological weapons, because anyone can rapidly produce them using the dark web.

"People often don't realize this, but fentanyl, carfentanil, nitazenes, medetomidine—all of these emerging synthetic drug threats are unique biothreats in that they're not like sarin gas, they're not like anthrax," Gage told Fox News Digital. "You can't go on the dark web and quickly formulate those substances. You can do that with these pharmaceutical-based agents that have completely caused havoc within the United States, and we're now starting to see that spread globally."

'ILLICIT' VERSION OF FENTANYL LINKED TO DEADLY NEW MEXICO INCIDENT THAT SICKENED FIRST RESPONDERS

ARMR Sciences is currently running a Phase 1/2 clinical trial to evaluate the safety of its experimental fentanyl vaccine and measure how effectively it blocks synthetic threats from reaching the brain.

Rather than waiting for an overdose to begin, Gage explained how the technology works:

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS

Galveston County authorities seized approximately one kilogram of fentanyl pills that investigators said were brightly colored and disguised to resemble ecstasy or MDMA. (Galveston County Sheriff's Office)

"We want our first responders to be as effective as they possibly can in the field," Gage said.

PRESIDENT TRUMP’S DRUG CONTROL STRATEGY SETS THE PATH TO END THE DRUG CRISIS FOR GOOD

With a new Democrat-controlled Congress preparing to take office, Gage urged lawmakers to treat synthetic drug defense as a "red, white and blue" priority rather than a partisan issue, noting that fentanyl "does not discriminate" by race or socioeconomic status.

Before expanding beyond the military to protect high-risk civilians like college students, Gage said safety and transparency must come first.

ARMR Sciences publishes its full formulation on its website and intentionally left out heavy metals—a move Gage tied to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s push to scrutinize ingredients, while also praising former Rep. Patrick Kennedy's efforts to overhaul addiction treatment facilities.

For Gage, whose mother struggled with addiction and who has lost friends to overdoses, the mission is deeply personal.

"Passion is born from internal suffering," Gage said. "No family should look over and see an empty chair at the dinner table. No kid should be hiding in their room because they're scared if a parent is suffering from an addiction issue. I want to prevent that happening from any American across the country. "

If you or someone you know is struggling with substance use, help is available 24/7 through the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357.

Brooke Curto is a breaking news editor at Fox News Digital in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s secret to staying fit at 57 starts with one simple workout routine
articles.excerpt:
Melanie Ramos, PVOLVE trainer, reveals that Jennifer Aniston trains three to four times a week, focusing on consistency and incorporating more weight training.

At 57 years old, Jennifer Aniston seems...
articles.body_text:
Melanie Ramos, PVOLVE trainer, reveals that Jennifer Aniston trains three to four times a week, focusing on consistency and incorporating more weight training.

At 57 years old, Jennifer Aniston seems to be defying the laws of aging — but it doesn’t come without hard work.

The "Friends" actress has been public about practicing PVOLVE, a functional fitness method grounded in movement longevity.

The workouts prioritize mobility and stability through twisting and reaching motions that translate directly to everyday life. Combining sculpting, cardio, and weight training, the method is designed to build muscle mass and support bone density.

10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG

According to PVOLVE trainer Melanie Ramos, what keeps Aniston looking and feeling her best isn't a specific workout buzzword — it's consistency.

"She's very consistent," Ramos told Fox News Digital. "She trains about three to four times a week doing PVOLVE, and she trains in all our modalities … She specifically is adding a lot more weight training into her routine."

Jennifer Aniston is pictured with her trainer Dani Coleman, VP of Training at PVOLVE. (Instagram @dani_bcoleman)

As people age, especially women, muscle mass begins to decline, according to Ramos, who serves as lead trainer at PVOLVE Soho in New York City.

"So, I think for [Aniston], the consistency and just adding that extra weight training really helps her look amazing," she said.

WANT TO AGE BETTER? RESEARCHERS SAY 4-MINUTE ROUTINE MAY HELP PREVENT DANGEROUS FALLS

According to research published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, only about 20% of women regularly engage in strength training, with many opting for aerobic exercise instead.

While walking offers major benefits for overall health, pairing cardio with simple resistance work can lead to significantly stronger heart and longevity outcomes.

Jennifer Aniston, pictured in 2025, has been adding a lot more weight training into her routine, a PVOLVE trainer shared. (Rodin Eckenroth/FilmMagic)

Rather than feeling pressured to commit to a full-hour workout to see results, Ramos advised simply getting started, adding, "Something that [Aniston] really prioritizes is even just getting 15 minutes of movement. "

Starting with "baby steps" – aiming for at least three workouts per week, even if they're short – will help you feel "like you can achieve the goals you want," the trainer said.

YOUR WALKING SPEED MAY HOLD A CLUE TO HOW LONG YOU’LL LIVE, STUDY SUGGESTS

"And then build more of that lifestyle habit where it feels that you need that movement every day," Ramos continued. "Movement is a part of life, and as we age, we have to look at how we're moving our body."

Exercises for mobility and stability can help aging adults maintain balance and independence, the trainer said. (iStock)

Prioritizing strength training and gradually increasing muscular load helps build lean mass and improve bone density, according to the trainer.

As the body naturally stiffens with age, Ramos noted, targeted mobility and stability exercises become essential for maintaining balance and independence.

To show how simple it is to get started, Ramos demonstrated three signature moves from Aniston’s routine — targeting mobility, strength and stability, using just a pair of dumbbells.

Melanie Ramos demonstrates a squat and curl exercise done by Jennifer Aniston in her workout routine. (Angelica Stabile/Fox News Digital)

Melanie Ramos demonstrates a squat and curl exercise done by Jennifer Aniston in her workout routine. (Angelica Stabile/Fox News Digital)

Modification: Bring the legs closer together for a smaller and softer squat.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Modification: If twisting is hard on the back, hug the dumbbell closer to the chest instead of over the shoulder for smaller movement. Limit the bend in the supporting leg.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Modification: Hold the weight with two hands, tucking the elbows in and bringing it up in an uppercut punch style.

Always consult a doctor or healthcare provider before starting any new fitness routine, especially if you have pre-existing injuries or medical conditions.

Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Tennessee can smell a CFP berth and fans are preparing for Lane Kiffin’s LSU to hear every decibel of hell
articles.excerpt:
Dan Dakich gives his take on the situation surrounding Sam Leavitt after he didn't stay on the field for LSU Alma Mater song following their loss to Texas.

KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — Lane Kiffin insists he w...
articles.body_text:
Dan Dakich gives his take on the situation surrounding Sam Leavitt after he didn't stay on the field for LSU Alma Mater song following their loss to Texas.

KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — Lane Kiffin insists he wasn’t challenging Tennessee fans ahead of Saturday’s showdown at Neyland Stadium.

The former Tennessee coach has a funny way of showing it.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

With the Vols chasing a College Football Playoff berth, and LSU arriving with little left to salvage besides pride, Kiffin has given an already combustible crowd another reason to crank up the noise.

LANE KIFFIN’S ROSTER FIGHT SET THE STAGE, WILL WADE JUST THREW A GRENADE IN LSU-SEC WAR WITH RJ LUIS

The Tigers’ loss to Texas last weekend ended their CFP hopes, to the dismay of over 100,000 LSU fans in Death Valley that walked out of the stadium in a state of shock.

Now, Kiffin brings his team to Knoxville with a chance to wreck Tennessee’s postseason plans — and a head coach whose history guarantees this won’t feel like an ordinary road game.

Sure, some players will take the challenge personally, but a lot of them are worried about where they will play next season, or trying to secure a new contract with the Tigers athletic department for 2027.

In other words, LSU is limping into Knoxville with a head coach that will once again be part of the show because of his short tenure with the Vols that came to a screeching halt nearly seventeen years ago.

Kiffin infamously spent one season at Tennessee in 2009 before bolting for his "dream job" at USC, a stint that ended with his firing on an airport tarmac after the Trojans landed back in Los Angeles from their game against Arizona State.

Tennessee fans haven’t forgotten the departure. And with their own playoff hopes on the line, they certainly don’t need a reminder to make Saturday's atmosphere uncomfortable for the Tigers.

Tennessee Volunteers coach Josh Heupel talks with George MacIntyre #12 during the first half against Texas A&M at Kyle Field on Nov. 14, 2026, in College Station, Texas. (ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Yes, we've seen a version of this story already. In 2021, Kiffin was roaming the sidelines at Ole Miss when all hell broke loose against Tennessee. Over the final few minutes of the game, with the help of a questionable call from the officials, Vols' fans made the Neyland Stadium field look like a trash bin.

Beer cans, water bottles, hot dogs, mustard bottles and a golf ball.

Yes, someone threw a golf ball that dinged Kiffin on the leg, which led to the infamous video of the former Ole Miss coach holding it up for officials to see.

TENNESSEE FANS DRANK $1.3 MILLION WORTH OF ALCOHOL BEFORE, DURING TEXAS GAME ATTENDED BY PRESIDENT

Will we see that type of hostile environment on Saturday?

The LSU head coach, who loves the attention, essentially challenged the Tennessee fan-base, even though he awkwardly mentioned that he wasn’t actually testing folks inside Neyland Stadium.

"But the Ole Miss thing, I’m not challenging Tennessee, I just don’t think you can top that from just the feeling of what that was like, just the anger and hatred because it was so recent that was in that stadium and that all being there at the start of warmups," Kiffin said on Wednesday's SEC teleconference.

"And again, I’m not challenging Tennessee. It sounds like I am, but I think once we’ve gone through that, I don’t think anything’s going to — I think this is more kind of, and it was last time, this was more kind of like fun. They’re mad, they’re yelling things, they’re saying things and it’s kind of fun."

LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin calls a play during a Southeastern Conference football game on Saturday, November 14, 2026 at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Peter G. Forest/Sipa USA) (Peter G. Forest/Sipa USA)

LANE KIFFIN ADMITS TO WAKING UP EVERY HOUR WITH RECURRING NIGHTMARE OF LSU'S LOSS TO TEXAS

OK, well you can bet your mortgage that Tennessee fans will gladly accept the challenge in turning Saturday into a ferocious environment that should have ESPN prepared to silence the "F---" Kiffin' chants that will undoubtedly reign down upon the field.

Besides the fact that this 2026 season has been a disappointment for LSU, it’s the aftermath that will gobble the headlines over the next month. What will Kiffin do in the transfer portal and high school recruiting? Which coaches will no longer reside in Baton Rouge after this season?

How much money will the 2027 roster cost the LSU athletic department and respective donors who spent nearly $50 million on players this past season, only to end up with four losses before Thanksgiving?

Those are questions Kiffin will have to answer in due time. But Saturday's showdown in Knoxville is about Tennessee's opportunity at being one step closer to clinching a spot in the postseason, with the Vols only remaining game of the season taking place next week against Vanderbilt.

Now, add the former head coach to this environment and you've essentially got a powder keg waiting to explode.

Or maybe not, at least according to some Tennessee fans.

"I think we got all of that out a few years ago. This one is about LSU standing in our way of making the college football playoff," Aaron from Johnson City, Tennessee, told OutKick on Friday night. "He'll always have his mustard bottle and golf ball game (2021 Ole Miss vs. Vols matchup). He loves the attention, but he probably should have worried more about his actual team this season than talking so much before his Twitter hiatus.

"I don't know what to expect, but I know my Vols are two wins away from the postseason. I can't imagine what he'll say if they (LSU) ends up winning. Heck, he'd probably return to Twitter for a day. But no, this one is about our Vols. He (Kiffin) just happens to be coaching LSU."

But, Kiffin doesn’t think it will match the environment from 2021, when he returned to Knoxville as the Ole Miss head coach.

"I'm hoping its crazier than the Alabama game, I know i'll be doing my part," Colton, from Dalton, Georgia, said on Friday night. "We had Kalen DeBoer feeling all sorts of weird along the sidelines, if you've seen that video.

"I really want this to feel dangerous inside that stadium. I'm sure somebody is going to sneak a mustard bottle into Neyland for ole times sake."

Oh, and I promise you that is what Lane Kiffin is hoping for, as he roams the LSU sidelines.

Before the 2026 season got underway, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel provided his fans with a challenge for Kiffin's return, even if said in a joking manner.

"Whether it's the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they've got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival," Heupel said at SEC Media Days.

Two wins away from the postseason. A stadium filled with 100,000 fans that will most assuredly live up to their hype of making it uncomfortable for opposing teams.

The Tennessee Volunteers take the field before their game against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Oct. 17, 2026. (Getty Images)

Oh, and a wounded dog is rolling into Knoxville with a football team trying to keep the locker room together for the final two games of the 2026 season.

"Like one of our players said, man, our dreams ended, let’s go try to end somebody else’s," Kiffin noted about LSU's mindset.

Would it surprise me to see LSU win on Saturday afternoon? Nope, not with that amount of talent on their sidelines and the amount of games they had in the bag this season.

No matter the outcome, it's going to get feisty in Knoxville.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: Bill Belichick's Tar Heels hold moneyline edge over Virginia in ACC college football toss-up
articles.excerpt: Joel Klatt joins Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes to preview the College Football Playoff, ask if Indiana is being disrespected as the 8th-ranked team, and the chances of Ohio State and ...
articles.body_text:
Joel Klatt joins Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes to preview the College Football Playoff, ask if Indiana is being disrespected as the 8th-ranked team, and the chances of Ohio State and Oregon making the tournament.

College Football has been wild lately. Every week, with the College Football Playoff rankings coming out, it seems like the entire sports universe is up in arms. Personally, I won’t even pay attention to it for another couple of weeks. It doesn’t make sense to get annoyed at the committee for selecting teams when we still have another few weeks of the regular season remaining. Two teams that won’t make the postseason, but should put on a good show this week, clash as North Carolina takes on Virginia.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

North Carolina is 5-5 for the season, and they’ve only gone 2-4 in ACC matchups. I do wonder at what point the Tar Heels will become a strong college football program. The expectation with the hiring of Bill Belichick was that he would turn the team into a contender. In Year 2, there hasn’t been a ton of progress. There have been some good games, but there hasn’t been a true statement win or consistent improvement. It will be interesting to see where the team goes from here and how they can improve. The best-case scenario this year is that they end up in a bowl game.

BILL BELICHICK EARNS FIRST WIN AGAINST RANKED OPPONENT AS UNC UPSETS NO 25 PITT ON ROAD

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick, center, walks off the field after losing to Duke in an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 22, 2025, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (AP Photo/Chris Seward)

North Carolina started the season overseas against TCU and won the game 15-10, then came back stateside and won the game 35-3 over East Tennessee. The Tar Heels' toughest stretch of the season was against Clemson, Notre Dame, and Pittsburgh. They only beat Pittsburgh, winning on the road over a ranked team, 21-17. North Carolina took down Duke, and then these past four weeks they’ve gone 1-3, with losses to Syracuse, Miami and Louisville last week. Billy Edwards Jr. has been decent under center for the team, but he is a senior, so the team will need to figure it out next year.

Virginia also enters today’s game with a 5-5 record, but they are slightly better with a 3-4 record in ACC play. The Cavaliers aren’t exactly a good football team or program, but the expectations are also a lot lower for them than for North Carolina. Just like the Tar Heels, they are hopeful to win the last couple of games in the season so they can get a bowl game. It isn’t likely to be a good one, but still, getting into one is a good sign for the program.

Virginia Cavaliers head coach Tony Elliott lifts the trophy after the TaxSlayer Gator Bowl between the Missouri Tigers and the Virginia Cavaliers on Dec. 27, 2025, at EverBank Field in Jacksonville, Fla. (Getty Images)

Their season started with a couple of wins against North Carolina State and Norfolk State. They lost at a neutral site to West Virginia before running their record to 3-1 with a win over Delaware. Since then, they’ve gone 2-4 with losses to Florida State, SMU, Duke, and Wake Forest. SMU and Wake Forest were both ranked opponents, and they lost both games by 10 or more points. Their other wins were against Syracuse and California, with both games at home.

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick speaks to his players during the first half of a college football game against Syracuse at the JMA Wireless Dome. The game took place in Syracuse, New York, on Oct. 31, 2025. (Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

The biggest issue for Virginia is that they are a bit one-dimensional. The Cavaliers have run the ball 388 times, and they’ve thrown the ball 288 times this season. I don’t think they are overly impressive when they throw the ball either. North Carolina is much more balanced with 304 passes and 306 rushes. I think that makes Virginia easier to plan for. I expect North Carolina to win this game, and it is essentially a toss-up. Give me the Tar Heels on the moneyline.

For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

Trey agrees UCLA is the best team right now...

articles.body_text:
Trey agrees UCLA is the best team right now...

This week doesn’t have a ton of great matchups on the agenda – at least not ranked matchups. There are certainly some fun games, but with all the teams rising and falling in the ranks this season, there were almost certainly some more important games scheduled before the season began. This one between UCLA and Michigan looks like it was probably expected to be a great game, but only UCLA looks like a good team this season.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The UCLA Bruins are 10-0 for the season and currently the fourth-ranked team in the nation. This hasn’t exactly been the toughest season for the Bruins, but they’ve won all the games, so you have to give them credit for that, if nothing else. They’ve only faced one ranked team this season, and that was over a month ago, when they went to Oregon and won 17-15. Somehow, Oregon is back ranked fairly high, so maybe that win should be viewed as a strong win. A few weeks ago, it looked a bit less impressive.

UCLA BRUINS UPSET OREGON DUCKS TO STAY UNBEATEN AND CHANGE THE BIG TEN CHAMPIONSHIP PICTURE

Bob Chesney leads the UCLA Bruins onto the field before their game against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Ore., on Oct. 10, 2026. (Getty Images)

Outside of that victory, the Bruins should at least be credited with not having had many close games. Last week, the team beat Illinois, but it was only by eight points. Every other game has been by 10 or more points. We probably should also give UCLA a bit of credit since they’ve had two different quarterbacks leading their squad. Ty Dieffenbach took over late in the Oregon game, threw a touchdown, and has been under center ever since. Nico Iamaleava, the starting quarterback to begin the season, went down with a season-ending injury.

The Michigan Wolverines enter the week with a 5-5 record and are just 2-5 in Big Ten battles. They’ve lost three of their past five games as well. They lost to Indiana in a very competitive game, then lost to Michigan State and Oregon. Their wins are over two teams that aren’t exactly impressive. They beat Penn State by three points, and then Rutgers by seven. They started the year fairly well with three straight wins over Western Michigan, Oklahoma, and UTEP. The losses were against Iowa and Minnesota.

Michigan Wolverines quarterback Tommy Carr (14) runs the ball passed Penn State Nittany Lions defensive back Marcus Neal (31) in the second half at Michigan Stadium. (Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images)

KYLE WHITTINGHAM ADDRESSES JOB SECURITY QUESTIONS AT MICHIGAN, MAKES MORE HEADLINES WITH UCLA COMMENTS

I really don’t have much nice to say about the Wolverines’ offense. Their starting quarterback, Tommy Carr, has two games where he has thrown for under 50 yards. The team is 1-1 in those games, so I suppose we should consider that impressive, but I view it as a concern more than anything. Carr took over for Bryce Underwood, but I don’t find either of them all that impressive. I guess they just wanted to give Carr a chance to perform and see if it would work out. Even the running game, once a staple, isn’t quite impressive.

Sammy Omosigho #10 of the UCLA Bruins and Jalen Woods #9 of the UCLA Bruins celebrate a fumble recovery during the second half of a game between the Oregon Ducks and UCLA Bruins at Autzen Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) (Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

As you can probably tell, I don’t really like Michigan. They do get this game at home, which gives them a bit of an edge, but I’m not sure that it matters all that much. UCLA does have a big game coming up next week, and the kiss of death this season has been getting a high ranking. I just don’t see anything good coming from Michigan and think UCLA will win. I’ll take the -3 with the Bruins and hope they can keep focused before playing USC next week.
